title: Rational parabolic subgroups and minimality
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $P,G$ be group schemes over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Use closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme], and extension to the algebraic closure [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. A homomorphism $i:P\to G$ is a parabolic subgroup if it is a closed subgroup inclusion, $P$ is smooth and geometrically connected, and there are a $k$-scheme $Q$ and a $k$-morphism $q:G\to Q$ such that $Q$ is proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], $q$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and for every $k$-scheme $T$ and $a,b\in G(T)$ one has $q(a)=q(b)$ if and only if $a^{-1}b\in i(P(T))$. Thus $Q$ represents the fppf sheafification of the right-coset presheaf: $q$ supplies fppf-local lifts and the displayed relation identifies exactly the right cosets. Properness includes finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A parabolic $i:P\to G$ is minimal if every closed subgroup inclusion $j:Q'\to P$ for which $i\circ j$ is a parabolic subgroup of $G$ is an isomorphism. The subgroup $P=G$ is allowed.
